info.title: Property manager tycoon and rent tracker

messages.text:
"Create a fun, colorful 2D Property Manager Tycoon game that also acts as a reliable monthly rent tracker for my 2 to 3 real-life apartment buildings.

Multi-Building @COMMENT_BODY@ Navigation Features:
- Start on a cute \"Neighborhood Map\" view showing all my buildings side-by-side (e.g., Building A, Building B, Building C), with an option to add, rename, or remove buildings.
- Display a summary badge on each building showing its total collected rent and total pending due amount for the month.
- Clicking a building zooms into a visual cross-section of that specific building with its individual apartment units and cartoon tenants.
- Include a \"Global Dashboard\" at the top of the screen showing the combined total rent collected and combined total due across ALL buildings.

Core Gameplay @COMMENT_BODY@ Game Loop:
- Each turn represents one real-life month. Include a global \"Advance to Next Month\" button that updates all buildings at once.
- Give me a \"Rent Collection Day\" event where coins pop up over tenants' heads across my buildings, and I can click to log their payments.
- Add fun gamification elements: Cash register sound effects when rent is paid in full, happy or worried mood icons over tenants, and a \"Landlord XP\" bar that levels up when I collect rent across all properties.

Exact Math @COMMENT_BODY@ Logic Rules (Very Important):
- Allow me to add, edit, or delete real tenants, assign them to a specific Building and Apartment Number, and set their exact monthly rent amount.
- For each tenant, track: Building Name, Monthly Rent, Amount Paid This Month, Previous Due Balance, and Total Balance Due.
- When I enter a payment, automatically subtract it from their Total Balance Due.
- If a tenant pays less than the full amount, keep the remaining unpaid balance as \"Due.\" 
- When I click \"Advance to Next Month,\" automatically add the new month's rent PLUS any leftover \"Due\" balance from the previous month into their new Total Balance Due for every tenant in every building.
- If a tenant overpays, carry the extra money forward as a negative balance (credit) for next month.
- Color-code each apartment door: Green if Total Balance Due is 0 (Clear), Yellow if partially paid, and Red if overdue.

Data @COMMENT_BODY@ Reliability Features:
- Include a clean \"Ledger / History\" screen with a filter to view either one specific building or all buildings combined, showing a simple table of past months, payments, and math calculations.
- Automatically save all data locally so I never lose my tenants' balances when I close the game.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

I'll build a static HTML/CSS/JS game. Need to serve via start.sh (default-start with index.html), and capture with playwright. Let's check playwright availability and port.

Plan: Build a polished single-page game with:
- Neighborhood map view with buildings cards (add/rename/remove), summary badges, global dashboard
- Building cross-section view with floors/units, cartoon tenants, door color coding, coins pop animations, sounds (WebAudio cash register), mood icons
- Rent collection day mode, click coins/tenants to collect
- Tenant CRUD, exact math tracking
- Advance month logic with due carryover, credits
- Ledger with filters, table of history
- localStorage persistence
- Landlord XP progression
- Fun colorful UI with CSS animations, no external assets (emoji-based cartoon tenants)

I should make it visually strong. Design: playful "Property Tycoon" with rounded cards, pastel gradient sky, buildings with windows/door units, bouncy animations.

Data model:
```
state = {
  version, month: '2026-11', monthIndex, xp, buildings: [{id, name, color, units: [...]}],
  tenants: [{id, name, buildingId, unit, rent, paidThisMonth, prevDue, credit?}],
  ledger: [{month, buildingId, tenantId, tenantName, rent, prevDue, paid, dueAfter, kind}],
  settings
}
```
Requirement fields: Building Name, Monthly Rent, Amount Paid This Month, Previous Due Balance, Total Balance Due.

Key math:
- On advance: for each tenant: prevDue = totalDue (which can be negative credit); new totalDue = rent + prevDue (credit makes it negative or reduces). Then paidThisMonth=0. previousDueBalance shown = carried amount. Hmm spec: "automatically add the new month's rent PLUS any leftover Due balance from previous month into their new Total Balance Due". If overpay credit negative balance: total due negative carries forward. So totalDue = rent + totalDue. previousDue = totalDue(before adding rent)? Display "Prev Due" as carried balance, total = rent + prevDue.

- When entering a payment: totalDue -= amount; paidThisMonth += amount. If payment > due, totalDue negative = credit.

Door colors: Green total<=0; Yellow if balance >0 but partially paid (paidThisMonth > 0); Red if overdue (balance >0 and no payment). Maybe also red if month advanced with due. That matches "Yellow if partially paid, Red if overdue."

Ledger: record per-payment event, plus month rollovers with math. Build rows: date/month, building, tenant, rent, prevDue, paid, due after, calculation note. Include filter all/building. Also show summary.

Rent Collection Day event: button "Collect Rent" triggers coin sprites appear over tenants with due, clicking each logs full payment with sound. Also individual "Log Payment" modal for partial payments. Should be possible to start collection day; coins pop over tenants across buildings on map and in building view.

XP: +XP per collection amount maybe 1 XP per $10, level thresholds. Bar.

Sound: WebAudio synthesized register "ka-ching" plus coin dings. Toggle.

Mobile responsive. Add demo seed data (3 buildings) with tenants. Persistence localStorage, with save indicator.

Let me be careful with amount of code, but complete. Vanilla JS single file maybe ~1800 lines. Let's structure index.html, styles.css, app.js. Static server works.

Let me check port and playwright.

Let's build. I'll design carefully. Screens: 1. Map view (`#mapView`): header global dashboard (title, month, XP bar, total collected/due badges), controls (Collect Rent Day, Advance Month, Ledger, Settings/Sound), neighborhood scene with sky, sun, clouds, road, building cards side by side. Each building card = CSS building illustration with windows, name, badges, occupancy, add/rename/remove menu. Add building tile. 2. Building view: breadcrumb back, building detail header with payment inputs? Cross-section with floors. Each unit shows door color, tenant avatar (emoji + style), name, rent, paid, due, coin pop animation. Click unit opens payment modal (log payment with quick buttons "Full", "Half", custom). For vacant units: Add tenant. 3. Ledger: filter building dropdown + month filter maybe, table, summary totals, empty state. Export? Not required. 4. Modals: tenant editor, building editor, payment, collection day results, confirm. 5. Toast messages. Game interactions: - "Rent Collection Day" toggles collection mode; coins appear over tenants with due > 0. Clicking coin collects full due for that tenant, sound + xp + confetti. Maybe a top banner with progress "3 of 5 collected". Also global collect across all buildings even while map view: clicking a building in collection mode? Requirement: coins pop up over tenants' heads across my buildings. Global event should overlay coins on the map building cards or force switch? Better: collection mode on map shows coins floating over each building card with amount, clicking collects one tenant's full due (or opens a collection panel listing tenants across buildings). I'll implement: clicking Collect Rent Day opens an overlay "Collection Day" sheet anchored bottom with all tenants across buildings and coin buttons, plus coins float over building cards on map; clicking a coin on a building opens its collection strip? Hmm complexity. Simpler coherent: Collection Day mode: - On map, each building card shows floating coin bubble total for building ("+$2,400"). Clicking it collects all due in that building? Requirement: "coins pop up over tenants' heads across my buildings, and I can click to log their payments." So we need per-tenant coins across buildings. Implement collection overlay panel: when active, a bottom tray shows all buildings' tenants with dues as coin chips; clicking a chip collects in full. Simultaneously on each building card, small tenant face chips with coin. Could be a lot. Maybe collection day modal full-screen "Rent Day!" with each building as a column and tenant rows with coin buttons. That is across buildings and per tenant. Plus coins animate on click. Good. But also unit view coins. Let's do: Rent Day modal overlay ("happy street") listing buildings columns, tenants with due, each row shows avatar and due and floating coin button "Collect $X". On click: ka-ching, coin fly animation to total, row updates, xp. Also "Collect all" button. Closing ends event, sets state.eventActive false. Additionally when in building view and event active, coins over units. Advance month: confirm modal showing math preview: new rent total, carried dues, credits. "Create a fun, colorful 2D Property Manager Tycoon game that also acts as a reliable monthly rent tracker for my 2 to 3 real-life apartment buildings.

Multi-Building @COMMENT_BODY@ Navigation Features:
- Start on a cute \"Neighborhood Map\" view showing all my buildings side-by-side (e.g., Building A, Building B, Building C), with an option to add, rename, or remove buildings.
- Display a summary badge on each building showing its total collected rent and total pending due amount for the month.
- Clicking a building zooms into a visual cross-section of that specific building with its individual apartment units and cartoon tenants.
- Include a \"Global Dashboard\" at the top of the screen showing the combined total rent collected and combined total due across ALL buildings.

Core Gameplay @COMMENT_BODY@ Game Loop:
- Each turn represents one real-life month. Include a global \"Advance to Next Month\" button that updates all buildings at once.
- Give me a \"Rent Collection Day\" event where coins pop up over tenants' heads across my buildings, and I can click to log their payments.
- Add fun gamification elements: Cash register sound effects when rent is paid in full, happy or worried mood icons over tenants, and a \"Landlord XP\" bar that levels up when I collect rent across all properties.

Exact Math @COMMENT_BODY@ Logic Rules (Very Important):
- Allow me to add, edit, or delete real tenants, assign them to a specific Building and Apartment Number, and set their exact monthly rent amount.
- For each tenant, track: Building Name, Monthly Rent, Amount Paid This Month, Previous Due Balance, and Total Balance Due.
- When I enter a payment, automatically subtract it from their Total Balance Due.
- If a tenant pays less than the full amount, keep the remaining unpaid balance as \"Due.\" 
- When I click \"Advance to Next Month,\" automatically add the new month's rent PLUS any leftover \"Due\" balance from the previous month into their new Total Balance Due for every tenant in every building.
- If a tenant overpays, carry the extra money forward as a negative balance (credit) for next month.
- Color-code each apartment door: Green if Total Balance Due is 0 (Clear), Yellow if partially paid, and Red if overdue.

Data @COMMENT_BODY@ Reliability Features:
- Include a clean \"Ledger / History\" screen with a filter to view either one specific building or all buildings combined, showing a simple table of past months, payments, and math calculations.
- Automatically save all data locally so I never lose my tenants' balances when I close the game.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown

## Objective
- Complete the standalone Property Manager Tycoon game and verify rent tracking across multiple apartment buildings.
- Test core workflows and inspect a JPEG screenshot captured at a viewport width no greater than 1280px.

## Requirements
- Neighborhood map with building add, rename, and remove controls; building-level collected/due totals; and a global dashboard.
- Building cross-section with tenants, balance-colored apartment doors, and tenant add/edit/delete.
- Monthly rollover must handle partial payments, arrears, overpayments, and credits accurately.
- Rent collection events, payment logging and history, sound effects, tenant moods, and landlord XP.
- Ledger/history filterable by building or all buildings; data persisted locally.
- Start with three sample buildings and ten tenants; support clearing sample data for a fresh start.

## Decisions
- Use standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript with browser `localStorage`.

## Work State

### Completed
- Fixed `buildingCard()` to use `occ.tenants` and `floors.length` instead of nonexistent occupancy properties.

- Added ledger month filtering and reset the month selection when changing the building filter.
- Implemented backup import with JSON, size, structure, ID, building, tenant/apartment, and ledger validation; valid imports prompt before replacing local data.
- Reset ledger month filtering when clearing all data.

### Active
- Align responsive ledger CSS with current `.ledger-table-wrap`, `.ledger-tools`, and table markup.
- Test payment math, partial payments, credits, rollover, CRUD, backup/import, ledger filters, and persistence.
- Launch the app, capture and inspect the requested JPEG at viewport width ≤1280px.

- (none)

1. Update responsive ledger styles to match current markup.
2. Run syntax checks and exercise rent, CRUD, backup/import, filtering, and persistence workflows; fix discovered defects.
3. Launch the app, capture a JPEG at viewport width ≤1280px, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Main app logic, ledger filters and backup import.
- `styles.css`: Responsive styles, including outdated ledger selectors.
- `index.html`: App shell and JavaScript/CSS references.

- `buildingOccupancy(b)` returns `{ tenants, units, occupied }`.
- `import-file` invokes `importBackup(file)`; the new validation and restore flow still needs testing.

## Objective
- Complete and verify the standalone Property Manager Tycoon game, including rent tracking across multiple buildings.
- Test core workflows and inspect a JPEG screenshot captured at a viewport width no greater than 1280px.

## Requirements
- Neighborhood map with building add, rename, and remove controls; building-level collected/due totals; and a global dashboard.
- Building cross-section with tenants, balance-colored apartment doors, and tenant add/edit/delete.
- Monthly rollover must handle partial payments, arrears, overpayments, and credits accurately.
- Rent collection events, payment logging and history, sound effects, tenant moods, and landlord XP.
- Ledger/history filterable by building or all buildings; data persisted locally.
- Start with three sample buildings and ten tenants; support clearing sample data for a fresh start.

## Decisions
- Use standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript with browser `localStorage`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Fixed building occupancy display, ledger filters and sorting, adjustment identification, responsive ledger styling, and backup import validation.
- Fixed startup initialization in `app.js`: load saved state or sample data, render, and persist the initial state.
- Verified `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`.
- Installed Playwright Chromium and started a local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002 --bind 0.0.0.0`.
- Browser confirmed the sample view renders with 3 buildings and 10 tenants at 1280px; no console errors and no horizontal overflow.
- Directly tested partial payment ($200 against $500 due), overpayment ($700 against $500 due), and month rollover: remaining $300 arrears became $1,300 due with $1,000 rent; $200 credit reduced $1,000 rent to $800; monthly payments reset and ledger entries were created.

### Active
- Test building/tenant CRUD, rent collection, ledger filters, backup import/export, and persistence.
- Capture and inspect the requested JPEG at viewport width ≤1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser tests on CRUD, collection, ledger filters, backup/import, and persistence; prior `playwright-cli click "Open Building A"` did not match a page element.
2. Capture and inspect a JPEG screenshot at viewport width ≤1280px.
3. Re-run checks and report results.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Application initialization, rent calculations, ledger, CRUD, and backups.
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout and ledger styling.
- `index.html`: App shell and asset references.
- `start.sh`: App launch helper; expects `RUNTIME_DIR`.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper; expects `RUNTIME_DIR`.

## Important Context
- Repository files are untracked and changes are uncommitted.
- The sample data starts in the browser’s current month; current system date in the session was November 2026.
- `advanceMonth()` carries balances forward and adds rent; `logPayment()` supports partial payments and credits.
- Earlier browser launch failures were resolved by installing Chromium and starting the Python HTTP server.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and verify the standalone Property Manager Tycoon game, including rent tracking across multiple buildings.
- Test core workflows and inspect a JPEG screenshot captured at a viewport width no greater than 1280px.

## Requirements
- Neighborhood map with building add, rename, and remove controls; building-level collected/due totals; and a global dashboard.
- Building cross-section with tenants, balance-colored apartment doors, and tenant add/edit/delete.
- Monthly rollover must handle partial payments, arrears, overpayments, and credits accurately.
- Rent collection events, payment logging and history, sound effects, tenant moods, and landlord XP.
- Ledger/history filterable by building or all buildings; data persisted locally.
- Start with three sample buildings and ten tenants; support clearing sample data for a fresh start.

## Decisions
- Use standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript with browser `localStorage`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Fixed building occupancy display, ledger filters and sorting, adjustment identification, responsive ledger styling, backup import validation, and startup initialization in `app.js`.
- Verified `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`.
- Browser confirmed the sample view renders with 3 buildings and 10 tenants at 1280×900, no console errors, and no horizontal overflow.
- Directly tested partial payment ($200 against $500 due), overpayment ($700 against $500 due), and monthly rollover: $300 arrears became $1,300 due; $200 credit reduced $1,000 rent to $800; monthly payments reset and ledger entries were created.
- Local server is responding at `http://localhost:3002/`.

### Active
- Test building/tenant CRUD, rent collection, ledger filters, backup import/export, and persistence.
- Capture and inspect the requested JPEG at viewport width ≤1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser tests for CRUD, collection, ledger filters, backup/import, and persistence; prior `playwright-cli click "Open Building A"` did not match, and a scripted `requestSubmit()` navigated to query parameters without adding the tenant.
2. Capture and inspect a JPEG screenshot at viewport width ≤1280px.
3. Re-run checks and report results.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Application initialization, rent calculations, ledger, CRUD, and backups.
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout and ledger styling.
- `index.html`: App shell and asset references.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper; expects `RUNTIME_DIR`.
- `screenshots/`: Currently empty; intended location for screenshots.

## Important Context
- Repository files are untracked and changes are uncommitted.
- Sample data is dated to the current browser month, November 2026.
- `advanceMonth()` carries balances forward and adds rent; `logPayment()` supports partial payments and credits.
- The previous `requestSubmit()` test did not alter the persisted sample data; the browser is currently displaying the neighborhood view.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording

  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording

  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page

  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and verify the standalone Property Manager Tycoon game, including rent tracking across multiple buildings.
- Test core workflows and inspect a JPEG screenshot captured at a viewport width no greater than 1280px.

## Requirements
- Neighborhood map with building add, rename, and remove controls; building-level collected/due totals; and a global dashboard.
- Building cross-section with tenants, balance-colored apartment doors, and tenant add/edit/delete.
- Monthly rollover must handle partial payments, arrears, overpayments, and credits accurately.
- Rent collection events, payment logging and history, sound effects, tenant moods, and landlord XP.
- Ledger/history filterable by building or all buildings; data persisted locally.
- Start with three sample buildings and ten tenants; support clearing sample data for a fresh start.

## Decisions
- Use standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript with browser `localStorage`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Fixed building occupancy display, ledger filters and sorting, adjustment identification, responsive ledger styling, backup import validation, and startup initialization in `app.js`.
- Fixed tenant creation being rejected when the selected apartment is empty; fixed submit-handler checks to use `form.getAttribute('id')` because the forms name their `id` field.
- Verified tenant add, edit (including rent adjustment/ledger entry), and partial payment through the browser.
- Earlier checks verified `node --check app.js`, `git diff --check`, sample view at 1280×900 without horizontal overflow or console errors, and payment/rollover accounting for arrears and credits.

### Active
- Finish CRUD tests for building rename/remove and tenant delete; test collection, ledger filters, backup import/export, and persistence.
- Capture and inspect the requested JPEG at viewport width ≤1280px.
- Re-run final checks and report results.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing of building CRUD, tenant deletion, rent collection, ledger filters, backup import/export, and persistence.
2. Capture and inspect a JPEG screenshot at viewport width ≤1280px.
3. Run final syntax/diff checks and report results.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Application logic, forms, rent calculations, ledger, CRUD, and backups.
- `styles.css`: Responsive layout and ledger styling.
- `index.html`: App shell and asset references.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot helper; expects `RUNTIME_DIR`.
- `screenshots/`: Intended screenshot location; currently empty.

## Important Context
- Repository files are untracked and changes are uncommitted.
- Local server is responding at `http://localhost:3002/`.
- Sample data is dated November 2026; browser `localStorage` contains sample data and prior test payment activity.
- Browser CRUD testing successfully added and edited `CRUD Test Tenant` (renamed `CRUD Edited Tenant`, rent $1,300) and recorded a $100 partial payment. Restore the original sample save before final checks using `sessionStorage.__beforeTest` if still available; it was set to the sample save before this test sequence.
